child_drafts.description_long: A federal judge temporarily halted the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau’s planned mass layoffs in April 2025. Reuters, in a report republished by Inc., said the bureau intended to dismiss roughly 1,400 to 1,500 employees, a reduction approaching 90% of its workforce. The court order prevented the dismissals from proceeding while the legal challenge continued. The source therefore documents a proposed reduction and judicial intervention, not that the entire workforce was actually terminated. The court proceedings also bear on whether the agency could continue work, so the proposal should not be presented as a completed shutdown. This April episode followed February work stoppages and preceded separate reports that some CFPB functions resumed. It should be recorded independently with the court’s temporary status made clear; the original broad claim that all enforcement matters were dropped requires a separate case-by-case review of agency and court records.

child_drafts.description_long: The Department of Health and Human Services announced a department-wide restructuring on April 1, 2025, including planned reductions at the National Institutes of Health. In a June 24 Reuters report, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said the department had brought back 220 NIH employees after a federal judge blocked planned layoffs. The report also described 722 CDC employees being reinstated, a separate figure and agency. The NIH number is Kennedy’s description of reinstatements; it does not establish that every planned reduction was reversed or that NIH staffing returned to its earlier level. The April announcement concerned a restructuring plan, while the June report described subsequent court-related reinstatement claims. The June account gives no basis for claiming that a particular number of infectious-disease scientists were fired or that all those employees worked on one research area.
